what: The lane's check was 'cargo check -p blaze-std --all-targets passes'. On origin/main (136432aa02) 'cargo +nightly-2026-10-27 check -p blaze-std' ends with 10 errors (contract clauses '-> (r: T) ensures', 'where const { .. }', core::reflect, three blaze features), so no change to bstd can be checked, linted or tested with cargo as it is.
cost: about an hour to build a stand-in; every bstd result of the lane is from the stand-in, not from blaze
cause: bstd uses blaze-only syntax (A10, D25) while cargo is the dev-loop builder and lanes may not start blaze on the Mac
whys: a bstd change could not be compiled by the lane
cargo rejects bstd's blaze-only syntax and the lane may not run blaze
rule blaze-builds-blaze makes cargo the dev-loop builder but bstd is written for blaze only
no tool gives a cargo-checkable view of bstd
the tree has two builders and one crate only one of them accepts, with nothing bridging them
class: a crate only blaze accepts cannot be verified in the cargo dev loop
prevention: harness/v2/bstd_cargo.py writes a cargo-checkable copy of bstd (contracts and where-const stripped, reflection stubbed) and runs check, clippy or test on it; how-to row bstd-under-cargo. State: in the tree on branch bstd-fallible-alloc. It is a stand-in, not the fix: the class goes when blaze builds blaze in the dev loop again.
workaround: copy crates/blaze-std to a git-excluded crates/zz-bstd-shim with the blaze-only syntax taken out and run cargo check/clippy/test -p blaze-std-shim; three tests fail there on the base commit too (tests::explicit::a_worlds_limits_are_the_ones_its_maker_said, tests::paths::a_path_never_escapes_its_directory, video::videotoolbox's encode test)
state: open: worked around by harness/v2/bstd_cargo.py (how-to bstd-under-cargo)
